clue.text: Gave beer possibly as the drink

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of gave beer could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone handed over a beer, which may count as the drink in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of GAVE BEER; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink, from tea to wine.

clue.text: The man receiving a lot

explanation.surface: A man takes delivery of a large quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The person receiving guests is their host, and a host is also a great crowd or multitude.

clue.text: Reluctant to write a few lines

parts.note: a verse is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to pen even a short note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to write' is a link phrase: write A plus VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse means being opposed or unwilling, a synonym of reluctant.

clue.text: Nasty beast imprisoning people underground

indicators.note: imprisoning means one piece holds the other inside it
nasty signals that the word beast is mangled into a different order

parts.note: people means men

explanation.surface: A vicious animal is holding captives below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' looks like a description of the animal, but it is the signal to rearrange; the surface's prison is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey of a building that lies below ground level.

clue.text: Pernickety individual

explanation.surface: A fussy person is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular means fussy and exacting, and also means single or specific, as in one particular case.

clue.text: Exceptionally sad, the endings may be

indicators.note: exceptionally hints that the words sad and the are treated out of the ordinary and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorrowful remark that the conclusions might be unusually sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' rearranges SAD and THE; 'may be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A death is the end of a life, so deaths are endings.

clue.text: Found another answer, being determined

explanation.surface: Someone worked out a fresh solution through sheer resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-solved means worked out again, and resolved also means firmly decided.

clue.text: The monster on low reversed

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'The monster on low reversed', does not yield DRAGON: no word gives DRAG or GARD for 'low', and reversing ON gives NO in the wrong place; likely an OCR or text error, unconfirmed by search.

clue.text: Made an exotic garland for the head

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the words made an are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone produced an unusual wreath to wear on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a poetic word for a wreath or chaplet worn on the head.

clue.text: Others take life easy

explanation.surface: Other people relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest means the remaining ones, and to rest is to relax.

clue.text: Land where tales are spun by the heartless

indicators.note: tales that are spun are told, and spinning also suggests the words being twisted round
heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed

explanation.surface: Property is a place where stories are told by the cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' turns THE into TE, and 'spun' rearranges TALES ARE with TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is property in the form of land and buildings.

clue.text: Get hold of the necessary equipment

explanation.surface: Someone acquires the gear needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle is to seize or grapple with, and tackle is gear or kit, as in fishing tackle.

clue.text: How royal personages come over in London

definitions.text: How royal personages come over in London

parts.words: How royal personages come over in London
parts.note: monarchs passing over something would be said to make the journey this way, and the phrase names a London district and railway station

explanation.surface: A question of how monarchs arrive in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: KINGS CROSS is a London district and main railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: The district is named, punningly, by monarchs crossing over.

clue.text: Additional players-not at all bright

parts.note: over can mean additional, as in left over
the players in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: Extra actors who are rather dim.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is clouded and dull, the opposite of sunny.

clue.text: The guy showing a high-flier the short way

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a bird that flies high
St is the short form of street, a way

explanation.surface: A man points out a soaring bird along a shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's name, and guy is a word for a man.

clue.text: Firm, because in the chair, but certainly on edge

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a chair is a seat
Co is short for company, a firm
as can mean because

explanation.surface: A company boss is nervous despite holding the chairmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' looks like nervousness but means at the margin of the land; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The seacoast lies at the edge of the land, by the sea.

clue.text: Stands for display in the theatre

explanation.surface: Market stands are set up for a show in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalls are booths for showing goods, and the stalls are the ground-floor seats of a theatre.

clue.text: Sort of jumper seen only on 16

definitions.text: Sort of jumper seen only on 16

parts.words: Sort of jumper seen only on 16
parts.note: jumper suggests a sweater but means a leaping creature, one found where the land meets the sea

explanation.surface: A kind of pullover worn only at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests the British word for a sweater, but here it is a small leaping crustacean of beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The creature is a tiny hopping crustacean living on sandy beaches.

clue.text: The more upstanding punter

explanation.surface: A gambler who is more honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Better means more decent or upright, and a bettor is a gambler, or punter in British usage.

clue.text: Sheepish creatures get a make-over by 16

parts.note: male sheep are rams

indicators.note: a make-over remodels something, so the words get a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sheep are given a fresh look beside the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-over' rearranges GET A. RAMSGATE is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town lies on the shore, by the sea's edge.

clue.text: Some get ahead here and hold on

indicators.note: some means only part of the run of letters in get ahead here is used

explanation.surface: Some people advance here and keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick to or cling, keeping a grip.

clue.text: Tip-top jewellery for the show-off

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A flashy person wears superb jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the' is a link; the def is the act of showing off, a public display.
explanation.definitionFit: An airing is a public display or exposure of something.

clue.text: Attending a big match, swear!

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A fan at a major game curses.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a top-level international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare on oath, to swear to.

clue.text: This will keep one in comfort to some degree

definitions.text: This will keep one in comfort to some degree

parts.words: This will keep one in comfort to some degree
parts.note: to some degree suggests partly but means at a set temperature in degrees

explanation.surface: Something that keeps one fairly comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: The device regulates heating to hold a chosen temperature.

clue.text: Sinister radicals

explanation.surface: Menacing revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for on the other side from right, and radicals are the political wing of that name.

clue.text: One goes after money when single

indicators.note: goes after places the first word after the second

parts.note: L stands for pound, the money

explanation.surface: A single person chases wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lone means solitary, alone.

clue.text: Difficulties can result from many increases in pay

parts.note: C is the Roman hundred, many
rises are pay increases in British usage

explanation.surface: Big pay rises can lead to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can result from' is a link; a rise is the British word for a pay raise.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are times of acute trouble or emergencies.

clue.text: Hired without point, which is huffily objected to

indicators.note: without means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: hired means rented
SE is south-east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Something hired with no tip is taken badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent is to take offence at something.
